q: Which of the following is a toggle key?
explain: Caps Lock, Num Lock and Scroll Lock switch a mode on or off. Ctrl, Alt and Shift are modifier keys.

q: Keys such as Ctrl, Alt and Shift, which change the action of another key when held with it, are called:
explain: Modifier keys combine with another key to change its action. Toggle keys, in contrast, switch a mode on or off.

q: In Microsoft Word, which shortcut selects all the content of the document?
explain: Ctrl + A selects all. Ctrl + S saves, Ctrl + L aligns left and Ctrl + M increases the indent.

q: Which shortcut opens the Font dialog box in MS Word?
explain: Ctrl + D opens the Font dialog in Word. Ctrl + F is Find, Ctrl + H is Find and Replace and Ctrl + B toggles bold.

q: Which shortcut is used to centre a paragraph in MS Word?
explain: Ctrl + E centres the paragraph. Ctrl + J justifies, Ctrl + R aligns right and Ctrl + L aligns left.

q: Which of the following pairs is correct for MS Word?
explain: Ctrl + K inserts a hyperlink. Ctrl + G is Go To, Ctrl + H is Find and Replace and Ctrl + J justifies.

q: Which Word shortcut opens the Find and Replace dialog?
explain: Ctrl + H opens Find and Replace. Ctrl + F only opens Find and Ctrl + G opens Go To.

q: Which of the following shortcuts is used to REDO an undone action in MS Word?
explain: Ctrl + Y redoes an undone action (or repeats a supported command). Ctrl + Z is Undo.

q: In MS Word, Ctrl + N is used to:
explain: Ctrl + N creates a new document, not a new page. Ctrl + O opens an existing file and Ctrl + P opens print options.

q: Which shortcut removes direct paragraph formatting in MS Word?
explain: Ctrl + Q resets paragraph formatting (not all character formatting). Ctrl + W closes the document and Ctrl + U underlines.

q: In MS Word, Ctrl + T is used to:
explain: In Word, Ctrl + T creates a hanging indent. In a browser the same keys open a new tab.

q: Which shortcut closes the current document in MS Word?
explain: Ctrl + W closes the current document. Ctrl + X cuts, Ctrl + Q resets paragraph formatting and Ctrl + O opens a file.

q: Which of the following correctly matches the shortcut with its action?
explain: Ctrl + Z is Undo. Ctrl + X is Cut, Ctrl + C is Copy and Ctrl + V is Paste.

q: Which shortcut opens Task Manager directly in Windows?
explain: Ctrl + Shift + Esc opens Task Manager directly. Ctrl + Alt + Delete opens the security screen, which also offers Task Manager.

q: On modern Windows, Ctrl + Alt + Delete mainly:
options: Locks the computer without a menu
explain: It opens a security screen with Lock, Switch user, Sign out and Task Manager. It does not directly restart modern Windows.

q: Which function key is used to rename a selected file or folder in File Explorer?
explain: F2 renames the selected item. F1 opens Help and F3 searches in File Explorer.

q: Which function key starts spelling and grammar checking in MS Word?
explain: F7 opens spelling and grammar checking. F5 opens Go To, F8 extends the selection and F9 updates fields.

q: Which function key toggles full-screen mode in a web browser?
explain: F11 enters or leaves browser full-screen mode. F12 opens Developer Tools in browsers.

q: In MS Word, pressing F9 will:
explain: F9 updates selected fields in Word (for example field-based dates). It does not update the whole document.

q: Which shortcut opens the Thesaurus for synonyms in MS Word?
explain: Shift + F7 opens the Thesaurus. Shift + F10 opens the context menu, like a right-click.

q: Which statement about starting Safe Mode is correct?
options: F8 at startup always works on every Windows version
On modern Windows, use Startup Settings after Restart and choose 4 or F4
explain: F8 opened boot options on older Windows. Modern Windows uses Recovery > Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Settings > Restart, then 4 or F4.

q: Which shortcut switches between open application windows?
explain: Alt + Tab switches between open windows. Alt + Esc cycles them in the order opened, Ctrl + Tab changes browser tabs and Win + Tab opens Task View.

q: Which shortcut copies a screenshot of only the active window to the clipboard?
explain: Alt + Print Screen captures the active window to the clipboard. Print Screen alone captures the whole screen.

q: Which shortcut opens the Properties of the selected item in File Explorer?
explain: Alt + Enter opens Properties. Alt + D selects the address bar and Alt + F4 closes the active window.

q: Which statement about a hard reload (Ctrl + F5 or Ctrl + Shift + R) is correct?
options: It erases all cookies and browsing history
It reloads the page while bypassing cached content
It closes and reopens the browser
It reloads the page using only cached content
explain: A hard reload bypasses the cache, which helps when a page shows an older version. It does not erase cookies or history.

q: Which shortcut reopens a recently closed browser tab?
explain: Ctrl + Shift + T reopens a closed tab. Ctrl + T opens a new tab and Ctrl + Shift + N opens Incognito.

q: In Chrome, which shortcut selects the LAST tab, even if it is not the ninth?
explain: Ctrl + 9 jumps to the last tab. Ctrl + 1 to Ctrl + 8 select the tab at that position.

q: Which shortcut opens Incognito mode in Chrome (InPrivate in Edge)?
explain: Ctrl + Shift + N opens an Incognito (Chrome) or InPrivate (Edge) window. Ctrl + N opens an ordinary new window.

q: Which key stops a web page from loading in the browser?
explain: Esc stops loading. F5 reloads, and Home and End move to the top or bottom of the page.

q: Which shortcut opens the browser's downloads list?
explain: Ctrl + J opens downloads. Ctrl + H opens history and Ctrl + D bookmarks the page.

q: Which shortcut restores the default zoom level of a webpage?
explain: Ctrl + 0 restores 100 percent zoom. Ctrl + Plus zooms in, Ctrl + Minus zooms out and F11 toggles full screen.

q: Which shortcut shows the HTML source of the current webpage?
explain: Ctrl + U shows the page source. Ctrl + Shift + I or F12 open Developer Tools, and Ctrl + P opens print options.

q: Which of the following opens Clear Browsing Data in a browser?
explain: Ctrl + Shift + Delete opens Clear Browsing Data, where you choose items and confirm. Ctrl + Shift + B shows or hides the bookmarks bar.

q: Ctrl + H opens Find and Replace in Word. What does it open in a web browser?
explain: In a browser Ctrl + H opens the browsing history; Ctrl + J opens downloads.

q: Which of these shortcuts has the SAME meaning (reload) as F5 in a browser?
explain: Ctrl + R reloads a page in a browser, although in Word it aligns the paragraph right. F5 itself opens Go To in Word.

q: What does F12 do in MS Word?
explain: In Word, F12 opens Save As. In supported browsers the same key opens Developer Tools.

q: Which Windows shortcut locks the computer?
explain: Win + L locks the computer. Win + D shows the desktop, Win + E opens File Explorer and Win + I opens Settings.

q: Win + P is used to:
explain: Win + P offers PC screen only, Duplicate, Extend and Second screen only. Win + S is Search and Win + V is clipboard history.

q: Which shortcut lets you choose from previously copied items?
explain: Win + V opens clipboard history. Ctrl + V only pastes the current clipboard content.

q: Which statement about Win + D and Win + M is correct?
options: Win + D toggles the desktop, while Win + M minimises all windows
Win + M toggles the desktop, while Win + D minimises all windows
explain: Win + D shows the desktop and pressing it again restores the previous view. Win + M minimises windows, and Win + Shift + M restores them.
